caveats: The opinion is unreported and its precedential use is limited.
Invalidity of an arbitration agreement because non-signatories did not consent is not classified as corruption.
counterevidence: The preserved misconduct/refusal-to-hear assertions were allegations in the protective petition, not adjudicated findings in the appellate disposition.

data.case_type: appeal from consolidated estate and arbitration confirmation/vacatur litigation
data.citation: No. 2119, September Term 2023 (Appellate Court of Maryland, filed Aug. 12, 2025) (unreported)
claims: alleged refusal to hear material evidence
data.outcome: Judgments of the Circuit Court for Baltimore City affirmed; the arbitration agreement was not enforceable against necessary non-signatories, the petition to confirm was denied, and the protective petition to vacate or modify was dismissed without prejudice.

evidence.claim: The circuit court held the arbitration agreement null and void because not all necessary heirs were parties, denied confirmation, and dismissed the protective vacate/modify petition without prejudice; the Appellate Court of Maryland affirmed. The record contains allegations of refusal to hear evidence and prejudicial misconduct, but the disposition does not establish those allegations as findings.

summary: Maryland appellate review of consolidated estate/arbitration litigation involving a Los Angeles Beth Din; the judgments were affirmed on contract/consent grounds rather than on the pleaded Beth Din misconduct allegations.
